dedupe_keys.name: regional earthquake loss estimation for 1 8 million san francisco bay area buildings simcenter workflow

description: This study presents an open-source, general-purpose scientific workflow for seismic damage simulation and loss prediction of urban buildings, referred to as the SimCenter workflow, which combines nonlinear time history analysis of multiple-degree-of-freedom building models with next-generation performance-based earthquake engineering. To demonstrate it, the authors simulated damage and predicted losses for 1.8 million buildings in the San Francisco Bay Area. Coverage: the Bay Area building stock. Access: article in Earthquake Spectra (2020); the journal page served a bot challenge on 2026-09-26, so facts come from the publisher's Crossref record. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-NC-4.0. Caveats: building models are simplified MDOF representations assigned from inventory attributes, and results depend on the scenario ground motions. Outcome: the open and modular workflow made city-scale nonlinear analysis practical and extensible to other regions. Simulation uses: regional earthquake damage and loss scenarios for emergency planning and insurance, and a template for other cities. Related records: NHERI SimCenter research applications, Pelicun and the Los Angeles woodframe functional recovery study.
